notes.meaning: Israel marched north along the road to Bashan, and King Og marched his whole army out to fight them at Edrei. Og attacked without being provoked, showing stubborn pride instead of learning from Sihon's defeat. When people ignore God's warnings to others, they bring ruin on themselves.

The Lord told Moses not to be afraid of Og, promising that the king, his people, and his land were already handed over to Israel. God commanded them to defeat Og just as they had defeated Sihon. Past victories from God give His people courage to face new battles.

God gave Og and his entire army into Israel's hands, and Israel struck down every enemy soldier. No survivors or royal heirs were left alive. God completely removed this hostile power so His people could move forward safely.

Israel captured all sixty of Og's cities across the whole region of Argob. Not a single walled town was able to hold out against them. This rapid conquest proved that God had the power to give them the rest of the promised land.

These cities looked very frightening, with high stone walls, double gates, and heavy bars. Israel also took many unwalled country towns throughout the area. No human defense can keep out God when He decides to act.

Israel completely destroyed the inhabitants of every city under God's solemn judgment, just as they had done to Sihon's kingdom. However, they were allowed to keep the cattle and household goods as plunder for themselves. God ordered this severe judgment on a corrupt culture to keep His people from being drawn into idol worship.

Israel took all the land ruled by the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River. This territory stretched from the Arnon gorge in the south all the way to Mount Hermon in the north. God gave them a massive tract of fertile ground to reward their obedience.

The great mountain of Hermon was known by different names among neighboring peoples. The Sidonian merchants called it Sirion, while the Amorites called it Senir. These ancient regional names help identify the northern boundary of the land Israel conquered.

The conquered region took in the cities of the high plateau, all the hill country of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as the border towns of Salecah and Edrei. Israel took full control of Og's entire kingdom. God completely fulfilled what He set out to do for them.

Og was the last surviving king from an ancient race of giant people known as the Rephaim. His iron bedstead was preserved in the Ammonite capital of Rabbah, measuring about thirteen and a half feet long and six feet wide. The defeat of such a gigantic warrior showed that no human strength can stand against the Almighty God.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern scholars translate the word for bed as a stone coffin or sarcophagus made of black basalt, which resembles iron.

notes.meaning: Moses divided this new territory among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh. Reuben and Gad received the southern region from the Arnon gorge into middle Gilead, while half of Manasseh was given northern Gilead and all of Bashan. Moses carefully marked out these tribal lands to establish God's rightful distribution.

Jair, a leader from the tribe of Manasseh, took control of the region of Argob up to the borders of Geshur and Maacah. He named these towns after himself, calling them the tent villages of Jair. This new name lasted long after the original conquest took place.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some commentators suggest the phrase 'to this day' was added by a later biblical editor such as Joshua or Ezra.

notes.meaning: Moses assigned the rugged hill region of Gilead to the family of Machir, a son of Manasseh. Machir's descendants had conquered this land and were granted it as their permanent home. God faithfully provides a secure dwelling place for every family in His flock.

The tribes of Reuben and Gad were given land stretching from Gilead down to the middle of the Arnon ravine, and north to the Jabbok River on the Ammonite border. Their western edge ran along the Jordan Valley from the Sea of Chinnereth down to the Dead Sea at the foot of Mount Pisgah. Moses fixed clear natural borders like rivers so the tribes would live in peace without arguing over water rights.

Moses reminded the eastern tribes of their solemn agreement to send their armed soldiers across the Jordan ahead of the other tribes. Their wives, children, and large herds of cattle could stay behind safely in the newly won cities. The fighting men had to stay and help their brothers until the whole nation had entered into God's rest across the river. God's people must never look out only for themselves, but care for the welfare of the whole community.

Moses told Joshua that he had seen with his own eyes how the Lord defeated the two powerful Amorite kings. Joshua was commanded not to fear any future enemies, because the Lord Himself would fight for Israel. Remembering what God has already done gives His servants courage to face tomorrow's challenges.

Moses poured out his heart in prayer, asking the Lord for permission to cross the Jordan and see the good land and the mountains of Lebanon. He praised God for beginning to reveal His mighty power and great deeds. It is natural to bring all our innocent hopes and longings to God in prayer.

The Lord refused Moses' request and told him not to bring up the matter again, because God was angry with Moses on account of Israel's past rebellion. Even though Moses was a deeply loved leader, he had to accept God's firm answer. God sometimes says no to our prayers for our spiritual good and to uphold His holy standards.

differ.view: God was not offended by Moses' prayer itself, but was upholding His earlier sentence against Moses because of the rebellion at Meribah.
God's anger mentioned here looks back to the earlier failure at Meribah rather than anger sparked by the request itself.

notes.meaning: God told Moses to climb to the top of Mount Pisgah and look in every direction to view the promised land. Even though Moses was not allowed to set foot in it, God granted him a wonderful view of the whole country. God softens His hard answers with deep mercy and comforting care.

Moses was told to commission Joshua, encourage him, and make him strong for the task ahead. Joshua was the leader appointed to guide the people across the river and lead them into their inheritance. It brings real comfort when passing leaders prepare and support the next generation of God's servants.

differ.view: Moses represents the law, which can reveal the inheritance but can never bring God's people into it, while Joshua pictures Christ bringing believers into true rest.

notes.meaning: Israel remained camped in the valley near Beth-peor, waiting for God's next command. They stayed there while Joshua was installed as the new leader of the people. God's people must learn to wait patiently in the place He sets for them until His plans unfold.
